task_description: Fix the real root cause behind 'the model picker shows nothing' (neither a reachable Ollama's models nor a cloud provider after adding a Kiro/Gemini key, with no visible error). Two bugs, one net effect: (A) frontend/src/state/providers.ts load() is never called on app startup or on chat-picker mount (only Settings > Providers & Keys calls it), so the chat picker store starts empty and stays empty; and (B) the backend never emits CoreEvent::ProvidersChanged, so saving a key/runtime never refetches. Fix: load the providers store once at app startup in app.tsx's existing top-level effect (mirroring how other surfaces load on mount), emit CoreEvent::ProvidersChanged via AppState.core_events after the provider-config mutation commands (route a - the sender is already available and used for MCP events), surface enumeration errors near the chat picker, and add an always-available Refresh affordance so failures are never silent (the user's build is the only live test rig). Stay on Tauri (no HTML5 rewrite). Do NOT touch embedded engine feature-flagging/release bundle or the embedded folder-scan rework. Update the spec. Do NOT push/tag/PR.

verification.summary: INTEGRATIONS_ONLY sandbox: crates.io + npm 403, no Tauri CLI, no frontend node_modules, no live Ollama/cloud endpoint - so cargo build/clippy/test, eslint/tsc/vitest, and tauri build are CI-ONLY and could not run here (recorded as skipped, pending GitHub CI after push). OFFLINE checks that DID run and PASS: per-crate `cargo fmt --manifest-path crates/tauri-app/Cargo.toml --check` and `... crates/orchestrator-core/Cargo.toml --check` (both exit 0 after edits). TEST QUALITY reviewed by reading the diff: (a) app.test.tsx adds a startup-load assertion (spy load called on mount) and tightens the single-subscription test to load-once-at-mount + twice-after-providersChanged - both fail if app.tsx's startup load() is reverted; (b) model-selector.test.tsx's Refresh test clicks the aria-labelled button, asserts invoke('list_available_models') fires, and asserts the fetched model becomes selectable via findByRole - fails if the Refresh button/load wiring is reverted; (c) commands.rs tests keep the core_events receiver (test_state_with_rx) and assert ProvidersChanged is queued for all eight mutations, plus a rejected-mutation test asserting nothing is emitted (exercises the emit-only-after-Ok contract). Hardening pass (follow-up to the 2026-09-09-061059 review): the eight positive backend tests now drive a per-command `*_and_notify(&AppState, ...)` seam (which runs the mutation then emits) rather than calling emit_providers_changed themselves, and each `#[tauri::command]` wrapper is a one-line delegation to that seam, so a dropped emit in a wrapper/seam is now a test failure; the tests assert exactly one ProvidersChanged per mutation and the rejected-mutation tests (cloud + embedded) prove no emit on the `?` short-circuit. A live tauri::State still cannot be built offline, but the seam is the exact code the wrapper runs. Verified theme.test.tsx renders <AppearanceSection/> not <App/>, so startup load does not affect it. Manual self-audit found no unused Rust/TS imports or vars introduced.
